purpose: Give Sentinel a compact mental model of network layers and traffic paths so observations are interpreted in infrastructure context.
interpretation_rules: A symptom observed at L7 does not by itself identify a cause at L3 or L4.
Source identity may be transformed by NAT, proxying or overlay routing; preserve the evidence source and trust boundary.
HTTP status describes an application/proxy outcome, not attacker intent.
TCP connection behavior, HTTP request behavior and application authentication behavior are different evidence classes.
Reverse-proxy logs describe traffic visible at the proxy boundary, not every packet reaching the host.
Container bridge addresses are internal topology and must not be interpreted as Internet attacker identity.
Overlay VPN addresses are a distinct trust/routing context, not ordinary public Internet addresses.
Correlate layers before escalating confidence; disagreement between layers increases uncertainty.
negative_knowledge: Do not call a 404, 401, 403, 5xx or timeout a network attack by itself.
Do not infer DDoS solely from high HTTP request count.
Do not infer compromise from a scan candidate.
Do not infer one physical actor merely because sources share a subnet.
